newsitem.title: USA: Fidelity's Beckwitt departs for Goldman Sachs.
newsitem.headline: Fidelity's Beckwitt departs for Goldman Sachs.

text.p: Fidelity Investments said it named Richard Habermann and Jonathan Weed to head its Portfolio Advisory Services business, replacing Robert Beckwitt, who is departing the firm to join Goldman Sachs & Co.
Beckwitt has headed Portfolio Advisory Services since March, when he was removed as manager of Fidelity's much larger asset manager funds in a massive reshuffling at the firm.

Habermann, who succeeded Beckwitt as lead manager of the asset manager funds, has had a long career with Fidelity, preceding Peter Lynch as portfolio manager of Fidelity's flagship Magellan fund. He also heads the firm's Asset Allocation Group, a team that also includes Weed.
Weed had been assisting Beckwitt in running the Personal Advisory Services accounts, which offer tailored investment strategies and require a minimum investment of $200,000.
Fidelity did not specify what Beckwitt's duties at Goldman will entail and a Goldman Sachs spokesman was not immediately available to comment.
However, a source familiar with the move said Beckwitt will act as co-head of Goldman's emerging market equities group and a vice president in its asset management division.
Ironically, Beckwitt's exposure to emerging markets, particularly Latin America, contributed to a sluggish performance by the asset manager funds towards the end of his tenure as chief.
